# Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#air)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-main.2446.pdf) · EMNLP 2026 proceedings, pages 55493-55504

**Reading coverage:** All twelve PDF pages, Sections 1-7, limitations, Appendices A-B, prompts, error examples, tables and figure data/descriptions.

## Research question

Single or superficially diverse SQL generations can omit plausible readings of ambiguous requests.

## Method

An anchor proposes an interpretation; adversaries seek alternatives subject to negative constraints and confidence gates. Candidate SQL is generated with execution repair, pruned when results agree, and used to synthesize contrastive clarification questions.

## Evaluation

AMBROSIA uses 440 test examples; AmbiQT uses a preprocessed validation set. Full-data versus schema-only conditions change generation context, while verification still executes against the full database. Metrics assess interpretation/output coverage, precision and perfect-set matching.

## What the results support

AIR improves schema-only F1 over the reported IntentRL comparison and reduces duplicate outputs. IntentRL retains better full-data AMBROSIA F1 and AmbiQT recall. The paper reports roughly 40 seconds per query for unoptimized serial API calls.

## Limits and qualifications

Different executed outputs prove query divergence only if proposed readings are valid. Identical current-instance results can hide semantic differences. No user study, clarification-quality assessment or cumulative dialogue-success evaluation is performed; fewer outputs are a burden proxy, not measured user effort.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Separates interpretation discovery from execution-based discrimination, while exposing the difference between coverage and completed clarification.
